newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) rise.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) rise.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Friday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose to 4.8 billion yuan from 2.4 billion on Thursday, with the 60-day contract the most active.
Traders said turnover increased today, with more borrowing by financial institutions to settle year-end accounts.

"Some non-bank financial institutions borrowed funds from short-term financial centres today for year-end settlement and their trading added liquidity to the market," a trader said. The centres are money brokerages run by the central bank.

"The 60-day contract was the most active today, because the contract period covers the days up to the Chinese Lunar New Year in early February," said a second trader. "The rebound of the domestic A share market was another reason for more active trading, with demand higher."
